message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade offer in Monopoly.

I'm in jail with $903 and three unimproved green properties. The offer is Baltic Avenue for $180. That would complete a brown monopoly, but the price is triple the normal cost.

The brown monopoly would yield $4 and $8 in rent without houses. Building three houses on each would cost $300 and raise rent to $90 and $180.

I've used two jail turns. I rolled 2+4 and 4+3 without doubles.

I might have to pay $50 and leave jail next turn. The trade is the current decision.

p3 just bought Baltic for $60 and built a house on Park Place for $200. They now hold Park Place, Boardwalk, and $8 cash.

Boardwalk also has one house. With $180, p3 could buy a second house on dark blue. Two houses on Park Place would rent $500 and on Boardwalk $600.

p3 cannot build a second house immediately. They would need $12 more cash, and they cannot mortgage their properties while houses are still on them. The trade would leave them with $188. I am now weighing whether the brown monopoly is worth $180 given my jail status and the current board threats.

p1 holds an orange monopoly with two houses on St. James and three on Tennessee and New York, totaling $1,350 in rent. p4 owns three railroads and cash of $1,630. p3's dark blue properties are manageable at $175 and $200 per house. My holdings do not form a monopoly without Baltic.

Baltic alone cannot match the orange monopoly's rent. Even a hotel on Baltic would yield only $450, which is less than a New York three-house hit of $600. The brown properties sit early on the board and see low traffic.

After the trade I would have $723 left. That barely covers one New York three-house hit with $123 remaining. I still need to pay the $50 jail fee eventually.

I am now considering whether p3 might already own both dark blue properties.

I own Mediterranean and p3 owns Baltic, so neither side holds a brown monopoly yet. p3 likely bought Baltic to prevent me from completing the set. Accepting the offer would give me a cheap cash engine with $50 houses and deny p3 any future brown play. The $180 price is a premium for a rare monopoly. The downside is that it would leave p3 with $188, just $12 short of another dark blue house.

A brown monopoly is the weakest set and would not bankrupt anyone quickly. I cannot collect rent from it while in jail. p4's $1,630 cash makes them a better trade partner for yellow or railroads. I should counter with a lower offer near $100 to $120.

A counter of $80 to $100 would leave p3 with $108, still too little for another dark blue house. I would keep $803, giving me a safer buffer against orange rent. If they reject and keep Baltic, it is nearly useless alone because rent is only $4.

I am now considering rejecting the offer entirely. p1 cannot afford to buy Baltic, and p4 would need Mediterranean as well to make it useful. Without that second property, Baltic is worthless alone. I could mortgage it later for $30 or keep it as leverage.

The brown monopoly is not my main win condition. I am now targeting the red set, which is entirely unowned and can be completed myself without trading. The greens are also a strong option if I buy both Pacific and North Carolina alongside my Pennsylvania property.

Baltic with two houses would rent $60, enough to bankrupt p1 with only $34 cash. Three houses would rent $180 and bankrupt both p1 and p3. This makes the brown monopoly a useful elimination tool in late game.

Building two houses on each brown property would cost $380 and leave $523. That could bankrupt p1 but not p3, and it would not stop an orange hit. Building three houses on each would cost $480 and leave only $423. That is too little to survive a New York Avenue three-house rent of $600. The brown monopoly is too expensive to build to a threatening level.

I should not spend below roughly $650 to $700 while the orange monopoly remains active. The probability of landing on a brown property is only 2 in 40, so I cannot collect rent from it while in jail. Accepting the full $180 offer would leave me too exposed to an orange hit. I will counter with a much lower price, around $60 to $80, and build houses later when my cash buffer is safer.

A counter offer of $100 would leave p3 with only a $40 profit, which they might reject. p4 could then buy Baltic from them for $100 to $150 and block my brown monopoly. I should not build houses now; the option value of owning the set is too valuable to waste.

I will counter with $100. That leaves me with roughly $800, which is safer than the $750 I had planned. I am not letting p4 acquire Baltic; that would permanently block my brown monopoly. I have twenty exchanges to negotiate.

A counter of $120 would leave me with $783. That is tight but still covers the orange hit and the jail fee. I should not lowball so hard that p3 sells to p4 instead. A price around $120 to $140 is safer. p4 does not need Baltic.

I will counter with $120 cash for Baltic. This price is above p4's likely denial bid, so p3 should accept. I cannot offer any properties because Ventnor blocks p4, Penn is my green starter, and Med is needed to complete the set.

I will keep the counter offer between $100 and $120. The $180 price would leave p3 with only $12 short of a second house, so I am not letting them build immediately.

I will start the counter offer at $100 cash for Baltic. This preserves my cash buffer while still giving p3 a quick profit after their $60 purchase. I cannot sell to p4 during this single decision; they would need to reject and propose to p4 on their next turn instead. The twenty-exchange window is strictly between us.

I will counter at $100 cash for Baltic. The public message will be friendly but firm, framing the offer as instant profit and a way to keep p3 liquid. I briefly reconsidered accepting the full $180, since a brown monopoly is a real asset and p4 previously paid $500 for Ventnor.

I will counter with $100 cash for Baltic. Unimproved brown rent is only $4 and $8, so the set generates no income until I spend over $100 on houses. I am ready to submit the counter_trade schema.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on Atlantic Avenue in the auction.

I have $903 and am in jail. I own Ventnor Avenue, so I already hold two of the three yellow properties. The auction is for Atlantic Avenue, which would complete my yellow set and block p4 from monopolizing it.

p4 has $1630 and would want to complete the yellow set. p1 has only $34 and p3 has $8, so they cannot meaningfully bid. The auction is effectively a battle between me and p4.

If I buy Atlantic, p4 would still need Ventnor from me to complete the yellow set. That would mirror my current position, but I would spend $260. If p4 wins, they already own Marvin and would hold the key to my yellow monopoly. I am now weighing the cash cost of bidding.

I am in jail with two turns already served. I may need to pay $50 to get out next turn. Orange rents are extremely dangerous. A bad roll could cost $550 to $600. My $903 cash is already tight. I had previously ranked Atlantic as a priority buy. I am now weighing whether to spend that cash on it or preserve it for orange protection.

Atlantic is ranked below reds, green completion, Baltic, and B&O. If I drop out, p4 could acquire it for as little as $35. That would give them two of three yellows and make Ventnor the key blocker. They might then try to buy it from me. Winning the auction would cost me cash that I need for orange survival.

Atlantic's unimproved rent is only $22. Without a monopoly, p4 cannot build houses there, so the property offers little immediate value. I am now weighing whether that small rent gain justifies spending cash on it.

Atlantic's value is mainly trade leverage and blocking p4 from completing the yellow set. A full yellow monopoly would be strong, but neither player can finish it without trading. If I let p4 acquire it cheaply, they would have more cash to pressure me for Ventnor later.

p4 already owns two of three light blue properties and three railroads. They have no monopoly yet. I am about to exit jail into the orange danger zone, so preserving cash is more important than bidding on Atlantic.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

**Evaluating bidding strategy**

I’m considering my bidding strategy and whether I should jump or bid strategically. Bidding $35 seems to eliminate poor participants, although p1 can still mortgage. If I bid $35, I could compete with p2 up to around $300. Jumping to $150 feels unnecessary, so I think I’ll stick with my $35 bid as a solid starting point. It could give me the leverage I need for this trade.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Buying Tennessee Avenue for $180 completes my Orange monopoly! I will have $619 cash remaining and can mortgage my non-monopoly properties to immediately build up the Oranges to 3 houses each.

Building 1 house on each of the three Orange properties first ($300 total) to comply with even building rules. Afterward I will build the second round of houses and consider mortgaging non-monopoly properties to reach 3 houses each.
Building a second house on each of the three Orange properties ($300 total), bringing them to 2 houses each and leaving $19 cash before I mortgage non-monopoly properties to push to 3 houses.

Mortgaging Water Works ($75) along with my Pinks ($140) will give me $234 total cash, allowing me to build a 3rd house on New York Avenue and Tennessee Avenue before p2 and p3 roll through the Orange stretch, while still keeping a $34+ cash buffer for the low-rent properties ahead of me.

Mortgaging St. Charles Place for $70 so I can follow up by mortgaging States Avenue ($70), bringing my cash to $234 and allowing me to build a 3rd house on New York Avenue and Tennessee Avenue right before p2 and p3 roll through the Oranges.

Building a 3rd house on New York Avenue and Tennessee Avenue ($200 total), bringing their rents to $600 and $550 respectively right before p2 and p3 roll through the Orange stretch, while leaving $34 in cash.
My Orange monopoly is now built up to 2-3-3 houses with $34 cash remaining and Vermont Avenue still unmortgaged as an extra $50 reserve if needed. Ending my turn.

Rejecting p4's offer of $240 for Vermont Avenue. Giving p4 the Light Blue monopoly when they have $1,630 cash would allow them to immediately build hotels or lock up 12 houses, whereas right now I hold the strongest monopoly on the board (Oranges at 2-3-3 houses) and p4 has no monopoly at all.

I only have $34 cash and cannot afford Atlantic Avenue ($260), so starting an auction is my only legal action. Importantly, p2 owns Ventnor Avenue and p4 owns Marvin Gardens, so neither can complete the Yellow monopoly solely by winning Atlantic Avenue at auction.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I now own a brown monopoly with MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE and BALTIC_AVENUE. I have $653 cash and can build houses on these properties.

I'm calculating house costs and orange rent. Even-building rules apply. I have a ways to go before hitting the orange properties again.

I'm evaluating unowned properties for purchase. Virginia Avenue is available and would complete a pink monopoly. The red properties are all unowned, making a red monopoly extremely valuable. Pacific and North Carolina would complete my green monopoly.

p4 owns two light blue properties and three railroads. p3 has a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property and only $108 cash.

Building houses on the brown monopoly seems unwise. Three houses each would cost $300 and leave only $353, while rent would barely exceed p3's cash. Two houses each would be even weaker. I'm weighing whether to build at all or hold onto cash.

Mortgaging all properties would yield only $350. That is enough to survive a $600 rent hit on New York Avenue, but houses must be sold before mortgaging. The trade-off between building and holding cash is now clearer.

Selling four houses on the brown properties would leave $453 cash, but mortgaging everything afterward would destroy the monopoly and leave me with only $203. Three houses would leave $353 cash, which is enough to survive a $600 rent hit after mortgaging Ventnor and Pennsylvania Avenue. I am still several spaces away from the orange properties.

Next turn, rolling 11, 12, or 14 from Pennsylvania Railroad would hit the orange properties. That is about a 17% chance. Tennessee Avenue costs $550 and leaves $103 cash. New York Avenue costs $600 and leaves $53.

I will end my turn and preserve the full $653 cash. Building houses on the brown properties is too risky given the 16% chance of a $600 rent hit on New York Avenue. I am now considering trades, particularly with p4 for a yellow monopoly in exchange for Ventnor Avenue.

Selling Ventnor Avenue to p4 would be extremely dangerous. That property is the gatekeeper to the yellow monopoly, and p4 has $1695 cash to build houses there. Without it, I would lose the yellow gatekeeper and face a heavily built yellow monopoly from p4.

I am now considering trading with p1. They own the orange monopoly and only $34 cash, so they might be willing to sell one of those properties to raise money. Purchasing an orange property from them would break their monopoly and remove the biggest threat.

Selling an orange property would force p1 to sell all eight houses first. That returns $400, leaving them with $434 and no monopoly. They are cash-poor and will not sell cheaply.

I am now calculating a concrete trade offer for New York Avenue. I would offer $400 plus nothing in exchange. I need to verify whether the game mechanics automatically sell houses when a property is traded.

Trading a property with houses on it is likely illegal in this engine, since buildings must be sold first. p1 would probably reject any trade for an orange property anyway, as those are their only lifeline. Their dark blue monopoly with one house each would cost $175 and $500 in rent.

p1 is currently on Atlantic Avenue and will circle around the board. Funding them would be unwise. p3 has dark blue properties but offers nothing of value to me. I will end my turn and preserve cash for the upcoming orange rent risk. A roll of 6 from my current position would land me on Kentucky Avenue.

I mapped the standard Monopoly board to verify exact space positions. From Pennsylvania Railroad, a roll of 2 lands on Community Chest at space 17, not St James Place. A roll of 6 lands on Kentucky Avenue at space 21. I am now checking which unowned properties fall in that range.

I had mapped the board incorrectly. From Pennsylvania Railroad, a roll of 3 lands on Tennessee Avenue for $550 and a roll of 4 lands on New York Avenue for $600. The chance of hitting either orange property immediately is 5/36, or about 14%.

Rolling 7 lands on Chance, 5 on Free Parking, and 11 on Atlantic Avenue. Atlantic costs $22 in rent because p4 owns two of three yellow properties without a full monopoly. Ventnor is already owned by me.

I cannot trade for unowned red properties. Proposing a trade would risk a counter-offer and accidental spending, so I will end my turn cleanly. Other players already know my cash is low.

I will keep my message brief or silent. I am now saving cash for Pacific and North Carolina, which cost $300 each. I will wait until after clearing the orange strip before building.

I cannot reach Pacific Avenue in one roll from my current position. I will save cash for red properties and B&O Railroad instead of buying greens this turn. p4 is also on Pennsylvania Railroad with $1695 and will roll toward the reds next. I am now checking the turn order to see who rolls before me.

p4 will roll from Pennsylvania Railroad before my next turn. They can buy the red properties I need first. I cannot block this. p3 is on Baltic and will roll next.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

An opening bid of $150 to $200 may still be outbid.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on Pacific Avenue in this Monopoly auction.

I have $653 and a brown monopoly. Pacific Avenue is the last green property I need for a full set. The current bid is $35, so I must raise it to $36. I am weighing whether to bid or drop out.

Mortgaging my brown properties would free enough cash to bid up to $150–$180. I will raise just over p4’s $35 bid and keep bidding until the price hits roughly $200, then drop out so p4 overpays for a denial chip. Pacific Avenue’s list price is $300.

A $36–$150 bid would be a steal if I can later acquire North Carolina. p4 has deep cash to sustain a denial bid, while p3 is capped at $100. I must keep enough cash to cover the $600 New York hit; mortgaging my brown properties would leave only about $53 free.

A $36 bid leaves $617, which covers New York without mortgaging. A $100 bid needs only the two brown properties mortgaged to reach $613. A $150 bid requires mortgaging Ventnor too, leaving only $643.

Mortgaging one brown property would remove the monopoly rent bonus, but that is harmless since those streets are unimproved. p4’s $35 bid looks like a deliberate denial signal, so I am weighing whether to raise just $36 or jump higher. If I do not push hard enough, p3 may bid up to $100 and then p4 will outbid me.

A $36 bid is small enough to trigger p4’s denial bid. I am deciding whether to raise sharply to $101 and eliminate p3, or stay cheap and test p4’s commitment.

A $101 bid would eliminate p3 immediately and leave room to raise further. Pacific Avenue alone is worth only its base rent of $26, since a two-of-three green set does not double rent under standard rules. Its real value is blocking p4 from completing a green set and positioning for North Carolina.

If p4 wins Pacific, they would hold the blocker on my green set and I would have to trade for it later. If I win, I can simply land on or auction North Carolina. Pacific is therefore more valuable to me than as a pure denial chip. p4 has deep cash and will pay heavily to deny me.

I have decided to bid $101. That price eliminates p3 and tests p4 at a meaningful level while staying within my $150–$180 ceiling. I am now weighing whether to let p3 bid $100 instead.

p3 would hold a dangerous blocker on my green set with only $100 cash and dark blues. p4 is the more aggressive holder. I prefer to own Pacific myself, then p3, then p4. A $101 bid eliminates p3 and leaves me facing p4 alone.

I cannot drop out now. p4’s $35 bid is a committed denial signal, and p1 warned that letting them acquire Pacific would leave a cheap blocker on my green set. I must raise the bid.

A $36 bid is too conservative. p4 has deep cash and will raise well above $100. A $101 bid tests whether they will pay a real denial price or simply probe.

A $150 bid is too steep. Pacific alone yields only $26 rent, so paying that much for a $26 return is poor value. The real worth is the denial chip: if p4 acquires it cheaply, I may never complete my green set without a bad trade. North Carolina is still unowned, so I can land on it or auction it if I win.

I am now calculating cash safety for a $90 or $101 bid. I am also checking the danger rolls from my current position on Pennsylvania Railroad, specifically St. James Place.

St. James Place is orange, not light purple. p1 owns it with two houses, so landing there would cost $140. I am checking the standard rent chart to confirm the exact amount.

St. James Place with two houses costs $200, Tennessee with three houses costs $550, and New York with three houses costs $600. From Pennsylvania Railroad, the first roll lands on St. James for $200, then Community Chest, Tennessee for $550, New York for $600, Free Parking, Kentucky, Chance, Indiana, Illinois, B&O unowned, and Atlantic Avenue.

A $101 bid leaves $552 cash. If I roll New York with three houses, I would be short $48, but mortgaging Med and Baltic for $60 covers the gap. Tennessee and St. James are easily manageable. The bid is safe.

I will bid $101. I am drafting a calm public message to avoid provoking p4 into an aggressive bidding war.

I will not telegraph my ceiling in chat. A short, noncommittal message is safer than a blunt declaration of $101 as my maximum. I am also weighing a moderate $50 bid instead.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. 2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Observe opponents and adapt.

- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid or drop out in this Monopoly auction.

I have $653 and am bidding against p4, who has $1703 and owns railroads, yellows, and utilities. Pacific would complete my green monopoly, but I still need North Carolina Avenue. The current bid is $151.

I will drop out. The $150 bid leaves $503 cash, which is enough to buy red properties or the B&O. I do not want to match p4's $1703 budget for a denial chip.

A green monopoly is expensive to build. Without North Carolina Avenue, the auction for Pacific would create a stalemate. If I win it, p4 will fight hard for North Carolina to block my full green set.

The orange threat from p1 is the real danger. St. James Place with two houses, Tennessee Avenue with three, and New York Avenue with three all yield high rents. This makes the green auction less appealing.

The earlier rent estimates are more accurate. New York Avenue with three houses costs $750 and Tennessee Avenue with three costs $700. My cash of $653 cannot cover either without mortgaging. I am checking the mortgage values for my brown properties to see if they can cover the orange threat.

The mortgage values in my notes are inconsistent. Ventnor Avenue should be $130, not $80, and Pennsylvania Avenue should be $160, matching standard prices. This confirms the orange threat is severe: New York Avenue with three houses costs $750 and Tennessee Avenue with three costs $700.

Mortgaging all brown properties yields $350 in extra cash. Combined with my $653 balance, I have $1003 total liquidity. New York Avenue with three houses costs $750 and Tennessee Avenue with three costs $700. Both are survivable after mortgaging. If I bid $180 for Pacific, I would have $473 left, which is enough to cover the orange threat.

Mortgaging all brown properties leaves a $37 shortfall for Tennessee Avenue with three houses. Standard Monopoly rules allow mortgaging to pay rent, so I can survive the orange threat after buying Pacific.

p4 is matching every bid to deny me the green set. If I jump to $200 they will likely bid $201. I am weighing whether that denial value justifies the cost.

p4 has two light blue monopolies blocked by p1, plus an electric company and a GOOJF card. They are not building a green set themselves; they are purely trying to deny me one. Their bidding pattern is to bid exactly one dollar over my last bid. With $1703 in cash, spending $200 or $300 on a denial chip is trivial for them, so they will likely keep matching until I drop out.

p4 will likely push the bid to $300 or higher. I cannot win this auction against them. Each increment raises their cost by exactly one dollar. The only value is forcing them to overpay. But if they drop out unexpectedly, I could win at a price I did not want. p1's warning about holding the blocker probably triggered p4's aggressive bidding.

I am reconsidering a small bid to extract cash, but only up to my $180–200 ceiling. Pacific alone pays base rent of $26, not doubled for a green monopoly.

I already own Pennsylvania Avenue, so p4 cannot complete a green monopoly without me. Buying Pacific does not block p4 from that set; it only advances my own path to completion. The auction is purely offensive, and the $180–200 bid offers terrible return.

If p4 wins Pacific, they would hold two greens while I hold one. When North Carolina Avenue comes up, p4 would bid aggressively to complete their set and block me. With $1703 versus my $653, I could not outbid them and would lose the green monopoly. If I buy Pacific instead, p4 would have no greens and I would hold two. The North Carolina auction would then become a direct contest for both of us.

I should not spend $200 on Pacific. That would leave me with only two greens and no cash to fight for North Carolina Avenue, where p4 could still deny me. I will drop out instead. The red properties are unowned and more valuable as a path to a monopoly.

Red properties are the best path to a monopoly. I will preserve cash for red landings and auctions instead of chasing an unattainable green set. p1 is nearly bankrupt with only $34, so he may go bankrupt and release his orange holdings.

I am now calculating the expected value of a $180 bid. Pacific is 60% of its list price for a property that only completes two-thirds of the second-best remaining monopoly. I need to weigh this against the risk of p4 bluffing out and forcing me to pay an inflated price.

The probability of completing a green monopoly is only 20–30% if I win Pacific, because p4 will deny North Carolina Avenue. Without Pacific, p4’s chance rises to 40–50%, since they have more cash to fight for NC.

A fully housed green set would yield $1275–$1500 in rent, which is devastating. Preventing p4 from building that set is therefore critical.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
The user is playing Monopoly as player 2.

Evaluating whether to buy Illinois Avenue for $240 or start an auction. The player currently owns a brown monopoly and no red properties. An orange threat from the opponent is noted.

Recalculating orange rent values with current house counts. St. James Place at two houses pays $200. Tennessee Avenue at three houses pays $700. New York Avenue at three houses pays $750.

Standard Monopoly rules confirmed. Buying Illinois leaves $413 cash. This survives a St. James hit of $200, but would be insufficient for a Tennessee or New York hit.

Mortgaging the four owned properties yields $350. Combined with $413 cash, this covers a New York hit of $750 with $13 left over and a Tennessee hit of $700 with $63 left over. Without buying, $653 plus $350 leaves $1003, which is comfortable for one orange hit. The decision hinges on whether to take that tight risk or preserve a larger cash buffer.

All three red properties are unowned. Purchasing Illinois would secure one third of the red group, leaving Kentucky and Indiana available for later.

Player 4 is the cash leader with $1552 and three railroads. They own Pacific Avenue, leaving North Carolina unowned. The green group is split between the two players. Player 4 is the biggest threat.

Player 1 has only $34 and cannot bid. Player 3 can bid up to $100 but cannot afford Illinois. Starting an auction would leave the property vulnerable to player 4, who could acquire it cheaply or block the red monopoly.

A red monopoly is one of the strongest in the game. Denying player 4 that group is a key strategic goal. The board layout from GO is being mapped to assess upcoming orange risk.

The board map is complete. Player 1 owns St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue with two, three, and three houses respectively. Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, and North Carolina are unowned. The player currently sits on Illinois Avenue.

The next roll from Illinois Avenue would land on Atlantic, Ventnor, Water Works, Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, or Pacific. Only Ventnor is owned by the player.

Rolling an eight from Illinois would land on North Carolina Avenue, an unowned property priced at $300. The next roll from here would also hit Short Line, which player 4 owns and would charge $100 for three railroads. The orange group is behind the player, so it cannot be reached on this turn. The turn order must be checked to see who moves before the player returns to those spaces.

Turn order is p2, p3, p4, p1. Player 4 just entered jail and may use a get out of jail card or pay $50. Player 1 is on Pacific Avenue and could land on the orange group next.

Player 1 cannot reach the orange group this turn. Player 3 on Connecticut can land on St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, New York Avenue, Virginia, the Pennsylvania Railroad, or Kentucky with a roll of seven through twelve. Player 3 has $100.

Player 3 could mortgage Park Place for $175 or Boardwalk for $200 to survive some orange rent hits. Player 4 is in jail and must either pay $50, use a get out of jail card, or roll doubles before moving again. The argument for buying Illinois is that it anchors the strongest mid-game red monopoly and would allow completing the set if Kentucky and Indiana are acquired later.

Auctioning would likely let player 4 acquire the property cheaply or deny the red monopoly. $240 is fair value for the best red, and an auction could force a higher bid or secure the space for player 4. The $413 cash balance is tight but sufficient for a North Carolina purchase, small rents to player 4, and avoiding orange hits until the next lap. The brown monopoly is complete but unbuilt.

Building brown houses is poor value because the $50 house cost yields weak rent. The prior strategy explicitly reserved cash for orange survival and the unowned reds, so buying Illinois aligns with that plan. Player 4 already controls two-thirds of yellows, light blues, and greens; acquiring the reds would make them unstoppable. The main counter-argument is that $763 total cash barely covers a New York Avenue hit of $750, leaving no margin for a bad roll or opponent house-building.

Player 1 cannot improve the orange properties because they only have $34, so the current rent levels will remain fixed. An auction would likely cost more than $240 or let player 4 acquire the property outright, since they will bid aggressively to deny the red monopoly.

The decision is to buy Illinois Avenue for $240. The player will retain $413 cash after the purchase. The upcoming roll from this position can safely absorb Short Line at $100, Atlantic at $22, Marvin Gardens at $24, and Pacific Avenue at $26. Dark blue properties are too far away to reach on a single roll. A roll of eight would land on North Carolina Avenue for $300, leaving $113 in cash.

B&O is one space ahead, so it cannot be reached this turn. The orange group is still a full lap away. Passing GO from here would yield $200. Building the brown monopoly is not viable because it would consume cash that must be preserved. A brief consideration of auctioning while player 4 is in jail was dismissed.

Player 4 bid aggressively on the Pacific auction while in jail, confirming they will fight for Illinois. Player 1's earlier message tried to manipulate the Pacific bid upward, which player 4 took advantage of. This makes securing the red group even more critical. The public message should stay strategic and confident without revealing cash concerns.

The official rent table confirms New York Avenue with three houses charges $800, not $750. This widens the cash gap to $13 after buying Illinois, making the orange group risk far more severe than initially calculated.

The official rent tables for St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue are now confirmed. Both charge $750 with three houses, not the $800 assumed earlier. This shrinks the cash gap after buying Illinois to about $63 instead of $13.

The official rent tables confirm New York Avenue with three houses charges $600 and Tennessee Avenue with three houses charges $550. The earlier private misremembering was wrong. After buying Illinois, the player would need $187 more to survive a New York Avenue hit.

Mortgaging three brown properties yields exactly $190, covering the worst orange rent hit. The player will likely pass GO before reaching the orange group, leaving enough cash to survive a New York Avenue hit without mortgaging.

The public message will be a brief, confident declaration that Illinois is being purchased at list price, with no auction theater. The private note will record the $240 purchase and $413 cash balance.
