The user is playing Monopoly as player 2 (grok-4.7).

I have $413 and four properties: Mediterranean, Baltic, Illinois, and Ventnor. I am considering a trade with p4 for the yellow monopoly. p1 has an orange monopoly but mortgaged St Charles, States, and Water Works.

p3 has a dark blue monopoly with one house each on Park Place and Boardwalk. p4 is in jail with $1552, railroads, and a GOOJF card. Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, B&O Railroad, and North Carolina are unowned.

Building houses on the brown properties would cost $50 each. The rent returns are too poor to justify spending $413 on them. That cash is needed for orange rent hits and to buy unowned properties like Kentucky, Indiana, B&O, North Carolina, and Virginia.

I am mapping the board positions. From Illinois (24), a roll of 2-12 lands on Atlantic (26) through Virginia (36). I am calculating the probability of landing on those spaces.

I will not pass GO from Illinois, so I miss the $200 rent. Landing on Atlantic costs $26 without a yellow monopoly. Ventnor is mine. Water Works is mortgaged by p1 and yields no rent. Marvin Gardens is p4's property at base $24. Pacific is p4's at base $26. North Carolina is unowned at $300. Pennsylvania Avenue is mine. The Short Line is p4's railroad.

The Short Line costs $100 in rent. I cannot land on the orange properties this lap, so I will pass them on the next round. I will not build houses on the browns until the orange risk is past and I have secured reds, Pacific, and North Carolina. I must never sell Ventnor or Pennsylvania Avenue to p4. I will contest Kentucky, Indiana, B&O, and North Carolina.

I am calculating exact orange rent amounts to plan cash reserves. St. James Place with two houses costs $200, Tennessee with three houses costs $700, and New York with three houses costs $750. p1 has only $34, so he cannot build more houses on his orange monopoly.

The private notes list Tennessee with three houses at $550 and New York with three houses at $600. Standard Monopoly rules would charge $700 and $750 for those same levels. This suggests the game may use a different rent table or the notes are approximating.

Standard house costs are $50 for browns, $100 for oranges, $150 for yellows and reds, and $200 for greens and dark blues. p3's one house on each dark blue property would charge $175 and $500 in standard rent. I cannot trust the earlier rent estimates because the game state does not contain the actual rent table.

p3 has only $100, so he cannot build more houses on his dark blue properties. p4 is the main threat because he has $1552 and a Get Out of Jail Free card while in jail. He still needs Ventnor for the yellow monopoly and North Carolina for the green one. My brown monopoly is weak, but owning Illinois gives me control over the reds. I am weighing whether to build houses on the browns.

I have decided not to build houses on the browns. One house per property costs $100 and yields only modest rent returns. I will keep my cash liquid for the red properties and other purchases. I am now considering whether to trade with another player.

I cannot trade Ventnor or Pennsylvania Avenue to p4. They would use those properties to build a yellow monopoly immediately, and they have $1552 to do so. I cannot trade for Kentucky, Indiana, or Virginia because those spaces are unowned. I need to find another way to stop p4.

St. James Place is orange, not pink. p1's pink monopoly is incomplete because St. Charles and States are mortgaged.

Trading with p1 is futile. He has only $34 and would not sell his orange monopoly. Trading with p3 is also pointless because he lacks properties I need.

I cannot trade away Illinois. It is my red foothold and the only way to complete the red monopoly. I will not give p4 a half-set of dark blue properties either. I will not offer bad trades in return for cash.

A bluff trade would waste one of my twenty allowed exchanges and reveal strategy. I will end the turn instead. I need to keep my $413 liquid for the red properties and B&O.

I need to survive the orange rent hits next lap. From Illinois, I will circle the board and pass New York in about five or six turns. If I collect rent before landing on the orange properties, my cash should rise to roughly $613.

The path from Illinois to the orange strip passes through Park Place and Boardwalk, each with one house. That would cost $175 and $500 in standard rent. The Short Line and Reading Railroad are also in that stretch. I will circle the board again next turn.

Mortgaging all five properties would yield roughly $420 in cash, giving me about $833 total liquidity. That should cover the $500 rent on Boardwalk with one house. I will not mortgage preemptively because unmortgaging costs 10% interest and those properties would stop generating rent.

I will not build the brown properties or trade away any blockers. I will end the turn and keep my message calm and brief, without revealing that I am saving cash for reds.

I am now considering a trade with p4. If I give Ventnor to p4, I would receive Atlantic and Marvin in return. That would complete the yellow monopoly for me and prevent p4 from building one.

I rejected the trade with p4 that would give Ventnor for Atlantic and Marvin. They would never accept trading away their two yellows to complete my yellow monopoly. I also considered offering Pennsylvania Avenue for Pacific and cash, but that would leave p4 with two-thirds of the green set instead of me.

I cannot trade for another player's houses. The game only allows cash, properties, and Get Out of Jail Free cards. I will not buy Vermont from p1 to block p4's light blue set. That would waste money and does not help me.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Third jail turn and both options are open, but waiting no longer helps. p4 is on Penn RR with $1560 and hits Kentucky/Indiana/Illinois/B&O on about half of rolls; p3 is on Baltic with $8 and will auction anything they cannot buy. I cannot reach Indiana+ from a single jail roll, but a paid exit is a guaranteed move now, before p4, and doubles still fail 5/6. $50 leaves $853. Orange hit odds are ~36% (SJ $200 / Tenn $550 / NY $600); all three are survivable once. Virginia (5) and Kentucky (12) are the only buys this roll. If I miss them, bid auctions hard for reds, Pacific, NC, B&O, Baltic. Do not sell Ventnor. Do not fund p1 or p3. Revisit Baltic only with surplus after the orange strip.

Counter to the $120 they floated. $80 leaves me $673, which still covers NY 3h ($600) with $73 left — tight but survivable, and Tenn $550 is fine. Brown monopoly is weak EV versus reds/greens, but p3 has $8, cannot build dark blue further, and may auction Baltic or die before I get another clean shot. Completing brown lets me house later if I survive the strip, and denies p4 a denial buy. If they reject, no cash spent. Do not go to $120. If accepted, do not build browns until orange risk is past and reds/Pacific/NC are secured or clearly lost.

Accept $100. Cash $753→$653 still covers one NY 3h ($600) with $53 left, and I already cleared oranges this lap (on Penn RR). Completes the only monopoly I can finish; $20 over my bid is cheap vs losing Baltic to a denial buy or p3 dying/auctioning it. Do not build browns yet — save cash for B&O ($200), Pacific/NC ($300), and the next orange pass. Do not sell Ventnor to p4.

On Penn RR (15). Next roll: 3 = Tenn $550 (2/36), 4 = NY $600 (3/36). $653 survives both ($103 / $53). Any build or cash trade makes NY a bankruptcy. Do not house browns yet — rents are weak vs that risk. p4 is also on 15 and moves before my next turn (p3 then p4), so they may scoop Kentucky/Indiana/Illinois/B&O first; nothing I can do. Save cash for reds ($220–240), B&O ($200), and later Pacific+NC to complete green with Penn Ave. Never sell Ventnor to p4. Do not fund p1 or p3.

Open at $1. Pacific makes me 2/3 green with Penn Ave; still need NC. p1 max $34, p3 max $100, p4 has $1703 and was just tipped to deny me. Cash $653; from RR a 4 is NY $600 (3/36) and a 3 is Tenn $550 (2/36). Can mortgage Med/Baltic/Ventnor/Penn ($30/$30/$80/$160) to cover, so not hard-capped at $53. Will go to about $150-180 if the price stays there. Above ~$200, drop and let p4 overpay for a denial chip. Do not trade Ventnor for Pacific alone. If p4 bids small, raise just over them next round.

Price out p3 ($100 max) and force p4 to pay real money or give me Pacific. $101 leaves $552; Tenn $550 is covered, NY $600 needs Med+Baltic mortgages ($60). Ceiling still ~$180–200 — above that drop and let p4 overpay for a denial chip. NC still unowned, so 2/3 green is worth contesting but not a war with $1703. Do not sell Ventnor.

Jump to $150, inside the $180–200 ceiling. p3 is out; p4 is matching to deny. $150 leaves $503 — still buys any red (Ky/Ind $220, Ill $240) or B&O, and a Tenn/NY hit is mortgage-survivable (Med+Baltic+Ventnor = $140). If p4 goes past ~$200, drop and let them overpay for a chip; NC is still unowned so 2/3 green is worth contesting but not a war with $1703. Reds remain the real win path. Do not sell Ventnor.

Drop. p4 is matching $1 over and has $1703; I will not win Pacific below their denial ceiling. I already own Penn Ave, so p4 cannot complete green without a trade I will not make. Pacific is only an offensive 2/3 chip that still needs NC, which they can also deny. Cash $653 is for orange survival (NY 3h ~$750 / Tenn 3h ~$700 need mortgages) and the unowned reds (Ky/Ind/Ill) plus B&O. Do not sell Ventnor. Contest NC only if the price is a true block, not a vanity set.

Buy at $240, cash $413. All 3 reds unowned; Illinois is the win path and list price caps what p4 can force. Auction just lets p4 deny or push me over $240. Orange rents stuck: p1 has $34 so no more houses. SJ 2h $200 covered; Tenn 3h $550 / NY 3h $600 need mortgages (capacity $350) but survivable. From pos 24 I cannot hit oranges this lap and may pass GO (+$200) first. Do not build browns. Contest Ky/Ind/B&O/NC. Never sell Ventnor or Penn Ave to p4.

Brown monopoly is the only set I can house. One house each costs $100 and leaves $313 — still buys a red ($220) or B&O ($200), and mortgage capacity (~$420) covers a dark-blue or orange hit. Unimproved brown rent is noise; even one house roughly triples it and starts a clock on p4 while they sit in jail. Even build required. Do not touch Ventnor or Penn Ave. Reds remain the real win path if I land on them.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $313 and just bought ILLINOIS_AVENUE. I hold one house on each of the brown properties. The only monopolies are brown. Opponent p1 has a dangerous orange monopoly with heavy houses and low cash.

p3 holds a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property. p4 has $1552 and is in jail, owning yellows and light blues plus railroads. I own Ventnor, so I have the yellow group; p4 owns Pacific, giving them the green group.

The bank still owns Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, B&O Railroad, and North Carolina. I have just finished my post-turn actions. I am deciding whether to end the turn, propose a trade, mortgage a property, build on the browns, or sell houses. I already built one house on each brown. I need to determine if I can afford to build more.

Building to two houses on each brown would cost $100 and leave $213. Reaching three houses requires another $100, leaving only $113. Four houses would need another $100 but would leave just $13. The rent returns from browns are too weak to justify the cash outlay.

I am on Illinois (position 24). I cannot land on the orange properties this turn because they sit at positions 11 through 19. The nearest orange is St. Charles at 11, which I would pass before reaching it. Dark blue properties are also out of reach this turn; the farthest one is Boardwalk at 39, and a roll of 12 would only land me on Short Line at 36.

I am weighing whether to build more houses on the browns. Reaching three houses on each would cost $200 and leave me with only $113. That cash is needed to buy the remaining bank-owned properties, which are priced between $200 and $300. I cannot afford both the brown upgrades and those purchases with my current balance.

I cannot afford the red properties. From Illinois I can reach B&O, Atlantic, and Ventnor this turn. I will land on Ventnor, which is mine.

I am mapping the exact spaces I will land on from Illinois. Water Works is mortgaged and pays no rent. Pacific is unimproved at $26, since p4 lacks a green monopoly. North Carolina is unowned and costs $300, which fits my $313 balance. Penn Avenue is mine. I am recounting the board positions to confirm the remaining stops.

Short Line is p4's third railroad, so rent would be $100. Park Place with one house costs $175, which I can afford. The real risk is North Carolina at $300, leaving only $13 afterward. Building more houses now would likely prevent me from buying either property.

I cannot land on any red properties this turn. Kentucky, Indiana, Virginia, and B&O are all behind me on the board. I am weighing whether to buy North Carolina as a strategic block against p4's green group, but that would leave me nearly broke. My strategy notes advise contesting NC only if it is a true block rather than a vanity set.

Opponent p1 is on Pacific (31) and can reach the brown properties in one turn. A roll of 10 lands on Mediterranean Avenue for $10 rent, and a roll of 12 lands on Baltic Avenue for $20. This makes building more houses on the browns a pressing defensive priority.

I am p2 at turn 56. The next players are p3 on Connecticut, then p4 in jail, then p1. p3 cannot land on the browns this turn because they sit behind them. p4 is in jail and will likely stay there or pay bail.

The expected value of upgrading both browns to three houses is only about six dollars. That is far below the two hundred dollar cost. The upgrade would be a poor investment for this single lap. It could still chip away at p4's large bankroll over the long run.

Opponent p1 cannot build more houses on the orange strip because they only have $34. From position 24, St. James is 32 spaces away, which equals a full lap minus eight.

I cannot reach the orange properties in a single roll from my current position. The closest ones sit at positions 16, 18, and 19, which would require rolls of 32, 34, or 35. That is impossible on one throw. I will need multiple turns to circle back around. I also cannot land on GO from here in one roll; it would take sixteen spaces.

I will not pass GO this turn. I will land on spaces 26 through 36 instead. The next turn I may pass GO from position 31.

I am checking trade options. I cannot trade for unowned properties. Pacific is expensive because p4 paid $151 for it. I own Ventnor but p4 owns Atlantic and Marvin Gardens.

I will not trade Ventnor to p4. Completing the yellow group would strengthen them too much.

Opponent p1 has an orange monopoly and a mortgaged pink strip. They also hold Water Works.

Opponent p3 owns a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property. Their cash is only $100, so they cannot build another house.

I am evaluating trade offers from the other players. p3 holds dark blue monopolies, which would be dangerous to acquire. p1 has a nearly bankrupt orange monopoly and will not sell it.

I ruled out selling houses because I just built them and would lose value. Mortgaging is also unappealing since it costs interest to unmortgage later. I am now reconsidering whether p4 might trade their railroads for B&O.

p4 cannot finish the light blue or yellow monopolies without trading with me. Completing the yellow group would let them build hotels immediately and destroy everyone. I must never give Ventnor to p4.

I am calculating how much cash each opponent needs to survive a $600 or $550 orange rent hit. p3 has only $100 and would need to sell both houses and mortgage Park Place and Boardwalk to survive. I have $313 and can mortgage my browns for roughly $200 total, which gives me a comfortable buffer.

Selling both houses on the browns and mortgaging them would raise total liquidity to about $783, which is enough to survive a $600 orange rent hit. p4 is rich and safe.

I still want the red properties, but upgrading the browns to three houses would leave only $113. That is too little to buy Indiana or Kentucky without mortgaging, and p4 has $1552 so they could outbid me in an auction.

I am now considering a trade for Vermont from p1. It would block p4 from completing the light blue monopoly and deny them an immediate building opportunity. That makes it a useful denial chip even though it is not a red property.

I am now drafting a concrete trade offer to p1: pay them $50–80 for Vermont. That would block p4 from completing the light blue monopoly and deny them an immediate building opportunity. I will need to spend cash that could otherwise go toward the red properties, but p1 may be willing to cooperate against p4.

I am now leaning toward ending the turn. The trade offers look unpromising: p1 needs cash more than I need Vermont, and p3 would not split their dark blue monopoly. Further house building is not worth the cash I would spend. I will pass GO and wait for a better opportunity.

I am now calculating the exact sequence of spaces p3 will land on from Connecticut. Virginia is unowned and costs $160, while Tennessee and New York are both orange properties that would bankrupt p3 immediately. This confirms that p3 cannot safely reach the red properties without landing on an orange square first.

p3 cannot afford Kentucky at $220 with only $100, so it will likely auction. p4 in jail can still buy Virginia and Kentucky if they roll out, since they have $1552.

p4 cannot reach Indiana from jail, but they could land on Virginia or Kentucky. p1 can pay rent on my Pennsylvania Avenue, yet the Short Line railroad would cost $100 and likely bankrupt them.

I traced p1's exact path from Pacific. They would land on Park Place and luxury tax, then Boardwalk, all of which would bankrupt them. Passing GO would give them $200, but they would still be broke. They cannot build more houses.

A roll of 9–12 from Pacific would let p1 pass GO and collect $200. That extra cash could let them build St. James to three houses, raising its rent from $200 to $550. I cannot stop them from passing GO.

Even three houses on the browns would not stop p1 from passing GO and building St. James to three houses. I will preserve cash and end the turn. A trade with p1 is unlikely to work, but p4 might pay a premium for Ventnor to complete the yellows.

I calculated that p4 could build five houses on the yellow group for roughly $752 in cash. Three houses on each property would generate rent of $800 to $850, which is enough to bankrupt any opponent who lands there. Trading Ventnor to p4 would therefore be a losing move even for a large payment.

I will keep my public message brief and strategic. I am also weighing whether the second house upgrade is worth it long-term: the extra rent from two houses on the browns would only cover the $100 cost after about two landings, and three opponents share that traffic.

The expected value of a second house on the browns is only about thirteen dollars per full circuit, so it would take roughly seven circuits to break even. That is too slow for this game, and cash is better kept for the red properties. A third house would raise rent by one hundred eighty dollars per landing, but it still requires already owning two houses.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I have $333 and a brown monopoly with one house each on Mediterranean and Baltic. I own no red properties yet. Opponent p1 has an orange monopoly with three houses each and only $114 cash. That opponent is the biggest threat.

p3 has a dark blue monopoly with one house each on Park Place and Boardwalk. p4 is in jail with $1501 cash and a large portfolio of railroads, yellows, greens, and utilities. I just bought North Carolina Avenue.

I block p4's yellow and green monopolies. I own Illinois, so the reds are my main win path. Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, and B&O Railroad are all unowned.

I will not trade Ventnor or Pennsylvania Avenue. Those properties block p4's monopolies.

Building two houses on each brown costs $100 and leaves $233. Building three costs $200 and leaves $133. One house on each brown currently yields $10 and $20 in rent.

Two houses on each brown yields $30 and $60 in rent. Three houses yields $90 and $180. Four houses yields $160 and $320. A hotel yields $250 and $450.

Three houses is the sweet spot. I need cash to buy Kentucky or Indiana if I land there. Orange rents are severe: St. James Place with three houses costs $550, Tennessee Avenue $700, and New York Avenue $850.

New York Avenue with three houses costs $750, four $925, and a hotel $1050. p1 cannot build a fourth house on any orange property because that would cost $300 and they only have $114. Their orange threat is capped at three houses unless they acquire more cash. I am on North Carolina Avenue, which sits before Pennsylvania Avenue and the Short Line.

Dark blue rent is manageable. One house on Park Place costs $175 and one on Boardwalk costs $200, so I can survive both hits with my $333. p3 has no cash to build more houses, and selling them would be required to mortgage. p4 is in jail with a Get Out of Jail Free card and $1501.

p4 has no monopolies because I block his yellows and greens, and p1 owns Vermont. That leaves him with a scattered portfolio of railroads and utilities. I am now considering trading with p1 for something useful, since his orange properties are the biggest threat.

Trading with p1 offers little value. They only have $114 cash and no red properties to give away.

p3 has a dark blue monopoly but zero cash. I would be giving them money to build more houses, which could bankrupt them if they hit orange or railroad rent.

p4 has $1501 in cash but owns no red properties. He cannot offer me the reds I need.

I will hold the blockers and try to land on Kentucky or Indiana. Building two more houses on each brown costs $100, leaving me with $233. That is enough to buy one red property at list price. Building three houses would leave only $133, which is too little for a red. I must also follow the even-build rule.

The ROI on brown houses is weak. Landing on either property is unlikely, and the jump from two to three houses costs $100 for only a modest rent increase.

I will build one more house on each brown. That costs $100 and leaves $233, enough to buy a red property at list price. I will not build a third house because that would leave only $133, which is too little to purchase Kentucky or Indiana without mortgaging. If I land on a red, I can mortgage Illinois for $120 or Ventnor for $100.

Mortgaging Ventnor for $100 would give me the extra cash I need to buy a red property. I can unmortgage it later if I want. Ventnor does not generate much rent while unmortgaged because I do not own the yellow monopoly.

Pennsylvania Avenue and Ventnor are pure blockers with modest rent. Three houses on each brown would raise rent to $90 and $180, which could bankrupt p3 or p1 if they land there. p4 is likely to circle the board after getting out of jail and passing GO, so he may hit these early spaces. The downside is that cash would drop to $133, preventing an instant purchase of a red property.

Liquidation capacity is the deciding factor. With two houses on each brown, total cash plus house sales and mortgages reaches $723. That barely covers New York Avenue at three houses, which costs $750. Building to three houses would leave only $133 cash, so liquidation would fall short of even the cheapest orange rent.

Two houses on each brown leaves $773 in liquidation capacity, which still covers New York Avenue at three houses. The reds remain the true win path, so I will not overbuild browns. Even three houses on each brown would only yield $180 on Baltic, which is too small to threaten p4's $1501 cash pile.

p4 cannot build a color-group monopoly without trading. He owns no pinks, reds, or B&O Railroad, so the only unowned properties he could acquire would not complete a set for him. That makes him completely dependent on trades with me or p1.

p3 has no cash. If they land on an orange, selling both dark blue houses yields $200, and mortgaging both properties adds another $375, giving them only $575 total. That is still below the $700 or $750 rent on Tennessee or New York Avenue, so they would go bankrupt.

St. James Place with three houses costs $550. A player can survive that hit with only $25 left and both properties mortgaged, but no houses remain.

p1 has $114 and three houses on each orange property. They can pay dark blue rent, but they cannot build a fourth house because that would cost $300. p1 wants to build more houses, yet their cash is too tight.

I will not trade away blockers or help p1 or p3. I am looking for a trade that benefits me, but I have no spare properties to offer.

I have no spare properties to trade. I will either build modestly or end my turn.

p4 is in jail, so he will not land on the browns for a while. p1 is on St. Charles, which is far from those spaces. The probability of hitting the browns is low, so building more houses offers little immediate benefit.

p3 is on the Pennsylvania Railroad, so he is far from the browns. I will keep my cash as a red purchase reserve and end my turn without building, trading, or mortgaging. I briefly considered whether p4 could ever acquire a green monopoly, but that path is dead because I hold Penn while he holds NC and Pacific.

p1 could build a fourth house on each orange property, raising rent to $750, $900, and $925. That would exceed my liquidation capacity of $823, so I cannot stop them from doing so. I cannot bankrupt p1 either.

I considered trading with p3 or p1 to weaken the orange threat, but they would not give up their monopolies. I also rejected trading with p4, because a yellow monopoly with hotels would cost $1500 and he has $1501 cash after his recent purchase.

Three houses on all yellows would cost $900 and leave p4 with $600. Rent for three houses on those properties is roughly $800 to $900, which would bankrupt me immediately. The green set would be even more devastating.

p4 cannot build three houses on the green set because that would cost $1800, leaving him with only $301. Two houses on each green property still generate dangerous rent of roughly $390 to $450. I will not trade Penn Avenue or Illinois, and I am reconsidering whether building two houses on the browns is worth the $100 cost.

The probability of landing on either brown property is only about 2.1% to 2.2% per turn. That makes building more houses on them a poor investment.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.

- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

The user is playing Monopoly as grok-4.

Evaluating a trade offer from p4. They want PACIFIC_AVENUE and NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE in exchange for $100 and VENTNOR_AVENUE. I have MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, BALTIC_AVENUE, ILLINOIS_AVENUE, VENTNOR_AVENUE, and PENNSYLVANIA_AVENUE. Their holdings include READING_RAILROAD, ORIENTAL_AVENUE, CONNECTICUT_AVENUE, ELECTRIC_COMPANY, PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD, KENTUCKY_AVENUE, and ATLANTIC_AVENUE.

p4 holds MARVIN_GARDENS, PACIFIC_AVENUE, NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE, and SHORT_LINE. Their cash is $730 after paying $550 in rent. They also have one get-out-of-jail-free card.

I own both brown properties with one house each, giving me a brown monopoly. p4 holds Oriental and Connecticut in the light blue group. I hold St. James, Tennessee, and New York with three houses each, forming an orange monopoly.

Accepting the trade would give me a green monopoly. I would own Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, and Pennsylvania Avenue.

p4 would also gain a yellow monopoly. After the trade, they would have $830 and could build heavily on yellows. I would only have $233, which is too little to build even one house on all three green properties. Mortgaging may be necessary to develop my side.

p4 could build five houses on yellows for $750, leaving $80 cash. Their yellows sit at spaces 26, 27, and 29, which are heavily trafficked before GO. I cannot build greens fast enough to compete.

I previously avoided trading Ventnor or Pennsylvania Avenue because either would let the opponent win with their cash. I now realize that giving them Ventnor completes their yellow monopoly, while they already hold two of those three spaces. I am looking for a counter-offer that would let me keep Ventnor and still acquire the green properties.

I realized that to acquire both Pacific and North Carolina, I must give up Ventnor. The opponent already holds two of the three yellows, so completing their yellow group is unavoidable. I am now weighing whether to ask for cash in addition to the green properties.

I considered offering more cash for one green property, but that would not complete my set. I also looked at giving Ventnor plus extra cash in exchange for something that would hurt them, but they do not hold much of value to me besides the greens. Rejecting the trade is now the most viable path. Keeping Ventnor blocks their yellow monopoly, and they cannot complete their green group without Pennsylvania Avenue.

The established strategy is correct. A built yellow monopoly would be worse than the current orange monopoly, and p4 has $730 to develop it immediately. I am currently on North Carolina Avenue (space 32), while p4 is on Tennessee after rolling doubles.

p3 is on Kentucky with zero cash and a dark blue monopoly. They are vulnerable to bankruptcy. p1 holds St. Charles with $664 and an orange monopoly.

I could build one house on a single green property for $200, leaving $33. That would yield modest rent. The brown monopoly is too small to generate meaningful income. I also need that $100 cash to survive against the orange monopoly. Undeveloped yellows cost only $22 each.

Mortgaging non-yellow properties could raise roughly $297 in cash. That would still leave p4 with only about $530 total, which is too little to build three houses on all three yellows.

Mortgaging all non-green properties would yield only about $373. That is insufficient to build even two houses on my green set, so I would end up with a barely developed green monopoly while p4 has a heavily built yellow group.

The trade is catastrophic. Two developed monopolies would destroy me. From jail, the orange and yellow groups are landed on before the green set. I am now deciding whether to counter.

I am now looking for a counter-offer that gives me Pacific and North Carolina without giving Ventnor. I considered trading Illinois for Kentucky, but that would not help me complete the red group. The opponent wants a monopoly, so they will not sell both greens for only $333.

Offering only Pacific Avenue for $200 would leave the opponent with North Carolina, so they would reject it. I considered offering Ventnor for both greens plus a large cash payment, but they might overpay for a monopoly. Even then, yellow houses cost $150 each versus $200 for greens, and they have more cash to build faster.

A counter-offer of Ventnor, Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, and $400 cash would leave the opponent with roughly $330 plus mortgage proceeds. They could build four yellow houses for about $600, yielding rents up to $330. I would have $733 to build three green houses for $600, leaving $133. The rent values are comparable at one house each, but they could build more.

A counter-offer of Ventnor, both greens, and $500 cash would leave the opponent with roughly $527. They could build three yellow houses for about $450, yielding rents near $110 to $120. I would have $833 to build four green houses for $800, giving me two houses on Pacific and North Carolina and one on Pennsylvania. That could be competitive. However, they are unlikely to accept such a large gap.

A counter offering Ventnor for both greens plus $200 still leaves the opponent with enough cash to build five yellow houses while I can only afford two green houses. No trade that gives up Ventnor is viable unless I receive enough cash to build hotels first, which is unrealistic given their resources and the lower house cost on yellows. I will reject the offer outright and avoid any counter that signals Ventnor is available. I am now considering a completely different counter-offer.

I considered buying Kentucky from them to complete my red group, but they paid $221 for it and will not sell cheaply. I cannot offer anything they need in return, so there is no leverage. The best action is still to reject the trade outright. I will keep Penn and Ventnor as blockers and avoid revealing desperation. A public message should be firm and consistent with my strategy of never letting an opponent finish a set.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.
