One house each costs $100 and leaves $313 — still buys a red ($220) or B&O ($200), and mortgage capacity (~$420) covers a dark-blue or orange hit. Unimproved brown rent is noise; even one house roughly triples it and starts a clock on p4 while they sit in jail. Even build required. Do not touch Ventnor or Penn Ave. Reds remain the real win path if I land on them.

Cash $313 is the reserve for reds (Ky/Ind $220), B&O ($200), and auction wars vs p4 ($1552). Another brown house pair costs $100 and drops me under red list price; 3-house build ($200) has better rent ROI but locks the only win path. Cannot hit reds/B&O/NC this roll (on Illinois). Do not sell houses. Never trade Ventnor (yellow mono for p4) or Penn Ave (green blocker). p1 on Pacific may pass GO (rolls 9-12) and rebuild oranges — cannot stop that. p3 may auction Virginia/Kentucky or die on oranges. End and contest those auctions.

Do not buy NC at $300. Cash $333→$33. Liquidation without NC ≈ $823 (cash $333 + sell 2 brown houses $50 + mortgages Med/Baltic/Ill/Ventnor/Penn $30+30+120+100+160), which covers current orange 3h (SJ $550 / Tenn $700 / NY $750). Buying adds only $150 mortgage value, net liquidation ≈ $673 — short of Tenn and NY. From space 32 a Chance/CC Go-to-Jail skips GO and puts me 6–9 from the oranges; dark-blue hits (PP $175 / BW $200 on rolls 5/7) also drain me before GO. p4 has $1652, owns Pacific, and will outbid me for 2/3 green — list price is the only cap, and it is too expensive. Auction, bid only if price stays ≤~$180–200 so post-buy liquidation still clears NY $750 (max bid ≈ $223 = 823+150−750). Above that, drop and let p4 pay. Never trade Ventnor (blocks their yellow) or Penn Ave. Reds (Ky/Ind still unowned) plus Illinois remain the win path; keep $333 to buy them. p1 may add a 4th orange house ($100) — even more reason to hoard cash.

Jump to $150, my walk-away. Mortgage value of NC is $150, so winning is liquidation-neutral vs passing ($823 either way) and flips green leverage: I hold 2/3 (NC+Penn), p4 stuck on Pacific. Cannot complete green anyway. Cash after buy $183 covers PP $175; BW $200 needs a small mortgage. I pass GO before any red, so +$200 restores a Kentucky/Indiana buy. If p4 bids $151+, drop — they have $1652 and will $1-increment forever. Do not trade Ventnor or Penn Ave. Reds remain the win path.

Walk-away was $150. p4 bid $151 and has $1652; they will $1-increment forever. Winning NC only gives me 2/3 green (with Penn Ave) I cannot complete, and it drains the cash I need for unowned reds and orange survival. p4 cannot finish green without a trade I will not make. Drop. Never sell Ventnor or Penn Ave.

Hold. Cash $333 covers a red at list ($220) and a dark-blue 1-house hit (PP $175 / BW $200). Liquidation ~$823 still clears orange 3h (SJ $550 / Tenn $700 / NY $750). Do not build browns: 2h costs $100 for weak rent; 3h costs $200 and drops me under red list. Never trade Ventnor (p4 yellow) or Penn Ave (p4 green) — either monopoly plus their $1501 ends the game. p4 has no set without a trade. Reds (Ky/Ind unowned + Illinois) remain the only win path. p1 may add one orange house ($100); still survivable. End.

Walk-away is list $220. Win = 2/3 red (IL+KY); Indiana still unowned, only real monopoly path. Cash left $113; BW $200 covered by mortgaging Ventnor ($100) or Penn ($160). If p4 bids $221, drop — they have $1501 and $1-increment forever. Post-buy liquidation ~$713 pre-GO / ~$913 after GO, covers orange 3h. Never trade Ventnor or Penn Ave. If I lose, same cap on Indiana.

Drop as planned. Walk-away was $220; p4 $1-incremented with $1501 and will do it forever. Winning at $222+ leaves <$111 and I still need Indiana ($220) to complete red — I cannot land on Indiana this lap (space 23 vs me on 32). p4 cannot complete red without Illinois, which I will not trade. Cash $333 is for Indiana denial/buy and orange survival (liquidation ~$823). Never trade Ventnor or Penn Ave. Next fight is Indiana: keep them from holding 2/3 red.

Reject. Trade gives p4 Atlantic+Ventnor+Marvin and ~$830 plus mortgage capacity to drop 5+ yellow houses ($150) immediately, then they roll again on doubles. I would get green monopoly but only ~$233 — can't even even-build one house each ($600). Naked/1-house greens lose to built yellows plus p1's orange 3-houses. Never trade Ventnor or Penn Ave. Keep blocking yellow and green; cash $333 is for Indiana denial and orange survival.

Reject. Giving Ventnor completes p4 yellows. They have $730 plus ~$485 mortgage capacity, so 2 houses ($900) immediately, then another roll on doubles. I get greens+Kentucky but only $333; 1 house each on greens costs $600 and still loses to 2-house yellows ($330-360). Naked greens are $26. p3 is on Kentucky, likely to hit yellows with $0 cash; bankruptcy to p4 could hand them Park Place/Boardwalk too. I already block their green (Penn Ave) and red (Illinois). Indiana still unowned. Keep $333 and Ventnor for orange survival and Indiana denial. Never trade Ventnor or Penn Ave.

message.reasoning:
I need to evaluate a trade offer and decide whether to accept, reject, or counter it.

The offer gives me $250 and the green properties for VENTNOR_AVENUE. My cash would rise to $583 and I would own a green monopoly.

I would gain a red monopoly with Illinois and Kentucky. p4 would own a yellow monopoly and three railroads, but their cash would drop to $480.

p4 can immediately build one house on each yellow property. The rent for Atlantic Avenue with one house is $110 and for Ventnor Avenue is $130.

Marvin Gardens costs $150 per house. One house on each yellow property totals $450, leaving p4 with $30 after the trade.

Mortgaging railroads, light blues, and utilities could raise p4's cash to about $965. That would allow two houses on each yellow property, yielding $330, $390, and $360 in rent. They also rolled doubles and will get another turn.

I would be short $17 to build one house on each green property. I cannot afford the $600 needed without mortgaging.

Mortgaging Illinois, selling brown houses, and mortgaging Kentucky would raise my cash to $863. That covers the $600 needed for one house on each green property, leaving $263.

Two houses on the green properties would cost $1,200, requiring almost all of my assets to be mortgaged. That would leave me nearly broke and vulnerable to p1's orange monopoly, which already has three houses on St. James, Tennessee, and New York.

The private notes indicate three-house orange rents of $550 on St. James, $700 on Tennessee, and $750 on New York.

The earlier private note incorrectly listed Tennessee rent at $700 with three houses. The actual game event shows $550, which matches standard Monopoly rules.

Standard orange rent values are $550 for St. James and $600 for New York with three houses. p1 cannot build additional houses on the orange set because St. Charles is mortgaged. Unmortgaging it would cost $77, which p1 can afford with their $664 cash.

p1's orange properties are the immediate threat. p3 holds a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property and no cash.

Standard dark blue rent values are $175 for Park Place and $200 for Boardwalk. p3 is broke on Kentucky.

The strategy notes warn against trading Ventnor or Penn Avenue because either would complete a monopoly for p4. Cash should be reserved to block Indiana and protect the orange set.

This offer is the best p4 has made so far. It gives me a green monopoly plus Kentucky and $250 for Ventnor alone.

A green monopoly is the strongest color group on the board after dark blue.

I would end with $583 cash, more than p4's $480. I would also own all green properties and block p4 from ever completing a green monopoly.

The main risk is that p4 can build one house on each yellow property immediately before rolling again. I cannot build one house on each green property right now because I lack the $17 needed without mortgaging.

Two houses on the yellows would yield $330 to $390 in rent, which is devastating. Two houses on the greens would require $1,200 and leave me vulnerable to p1's orange set.

Naked green properties would only collect $26 to $28 per roll. p4 will still build on the yellows before rolling again.

I have consistently refused to give p4 a monopoly when they have another turn and building cash available.

If p4 builds houses on the yellows, p3 could land there and bankrupt. That would hand Park Place and Boardwalk to p4.

Turn order is p1, p2, p3, p4. p4 rolled on turn 63. p1 will roll next. Then p2.

p4 rolled doubles, so they will continue their turn after this decision. They may build two houses on the yellows and roll again before p1, p2, and p3 get their turns.

p3 is stuck on Kentucky with no cash and one house on each dark blue property. If p4 builds two houses and rolls, p3 could land there and bankrupt.

I am now considering a counter-offer instead of rejecting the deal outright.

I am trying to design a counter-offer that keeps the greens but prevents p4 from building a yellow monopoly before they roll again. I cannot constrain their building actions, so I need to find another way to block them.

One idea is to ask for more cash in exchange for the greens and Kentucky. Another is to remove Ventnor from the deal entirely, which would stop them from completing a yellow monopoly. However, giving up Penn Avenue would complete their green set, so that is not viable.

I only have Ventnor and Penn Avenue as pieces they want, and both are too risky to trade away.

A counter-offer demanding $700 cash for Ventnor would leave p4 with only $30. That is below the $450 needed to build one house on each yellow property, so they could not improve their yellows before rolling again.

I would end up with a green monopoly and about $1,033 in cash, enough to build one house on each green property and still have money left over.

The numerical value of the deal is lopsided: p4 would receive roughly $1,840 worth of property and cash for a $260 Ventnor. They might accept it anyway because completing a yellow monopoly is their primary goal.

Mortgaging every non-yellow asset would raise p4's cash to about $515. That is still enough to build one house on each yellow property and leave them with $65. I need to demand more cash so they cannot afford even that minimal improvement.

Mortgaging every non-yellow property still leaves p4 with $485, which exceeds the $450 needed to build one house on each yellow. To block them from improving, I should also take some of their mortgageable assets in the trade, such as railroads or utilities. A counter-offer could give Ventnor for Pacific, North Carolina, Kentucky, and enough other assets to shrink their mortgage pool below the building threshold.

A yellow monopoly with one house still yields $110 to $130 in rent, and p4 would roll again. They could rebuild cash and add houses on subsequent turns.

The core problem is that giving p4 any monopoly while they have cash and an extra roll is how I lose. Greens are better long-term, but I cannot develop them fast enough to match their speed.

If both players hold monopolies, the one who builds fastest wins. p1's orange set remains a constant threat.

p4's next roll from Tennessee could land on my greens, New York, or Indiana. They can build yellows faster and move first, so I cannot catch up.

Rejecting the trade would leave p4 with Kentucky. They might then buy Indiana for $220, giving them two of three red properties and leaving me with Illinois as a blocker. I would still refuse to trade Illinois, so the red set remains blocked. Ventnor would continue blocking their yellow monopoly.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I am p2 with $233 cash. I own two red properties with one house each. The other three properties have no houses.

p1 is in jail with $364 and an orange monopoly. p3 has a dark blue set with one house on Boardwalk and cash of $76. p4 owns three railroads and $754.

I own the light blue, yellow, and green monopolies. I hold one get-out-of-jail card. Unowned properties include Virginia Avenue, Indiana Avenue, and B&O Railroad. I will not trade Ventnor, Penn Ave, or Illinois because they block p4's monopolies. The red set remains my primary win path.

Liquidating all buildings and mortgaging properties would raise cash to roughly $723. That still falls short of covering p1's four-house orange rent. Rolling from the income tax space lands on Oriental through St. Charles, so I cannot reach the orange monopolies this turn.

p1 is in jail but still collects rent while there, so the orange monopoly remains dangerous. p3 owns a dark blue set with one house on Boardwalk and cash of only $76. Boardwalk with one house pays $200, and Park Place with one house pays $175.

p3 previously sold a house on Park Place to pay rent. They cannot build another house on Boardwalk until Park Place has one, so their dark blue set is currently weak. p4 has $754 and sits on Pacific Avenue. They have been offering increasingly for Ventnor, but I rejected those offers because they would immediately build the yellow monopoly and crush everyone.

I am weighing whether to trade. The safest choice is ending the turn and keeping p4 blocked. Building more houses on the brown properties would drain cash I need for survival and Indiana denial, and opponents rarely land there anyway.

p1 has $364, which is enough to hotel all three orange properties. They were sent to jail on turn 69, so they may have already built before ending their turn.

p1 cannot hotel the orange properties now because they are in jail. They would need to build during their next turn, which is post-turn or pre-roll. I have no way to stop them from doing so.

p3 is nearly broke with an undeveloped dark blue set. If they go bankrupt to p1's orange monopolies, p1 would gain both Park Place and Boardwalk.

Neither I nor p4 can reach the orange properties this turn or next. The distance from my current space to St. James is roughly 22 spaces, and from p4's Pacific Avenue it is about 35 spaces.

I am checking the standard Monopoly board layout to verify exact space numbers. p3 sits on Marvin Gardens (space 29), which is adjacent to the orange properties at spaces 26 through 29.

I had the orange property positions wrong. The correct spaces are St. James Place at 16, Tennessee at 18, and New York at 19. My earlier assumption that p3 was adjacent to the orange monopolies was incorrect.

Rolling a 12 from space 4 lands on St. James Place, which would cost $750 in rent. Even liquidating all buildings and mortgaging every property only raises cash to $723, so that risk is fatal. A roll of 11 would hit the Pennsylvania Railroad instead, which is manageable.

The St. James Place risk is too small to justify a bad trade. p4 will not land on the orange monopolies this turn, but they could hit my Pennsylvania Avenue for $26 or my browns if they pass GO.

I cannot build a full brown monopoly. Two more houses on each property would cost $200, leaving only $33. The brown set is too weak to threaten p4.

A brown monopoly would still leave me cash-broke if I hit rent. The red set is blocked because p4 owns Kentucky and needs Indiana from me. The yellow set is also unreachable since p4 holds both Atlantic and Marvin.

I will not complete the yellow or green monopolies for p4. A green monopoly would cost $200 per house, and I cannot afford to build on it with only $233. Without houses, the rent would be too weak to threaten anyone. I am now considering a trade with p3.

p3 will not trade their dark blue monopoly for anything. I cannot afford to develop it, and giving up my blockers would let p4 complete a yellow or green set.

I am now considering a trade with p1. They own Vermont and the orange monopoly, but their pink set is incomplete because St. Charles and States are mortgaged. Virginia Avenue is unowned, so they cannot finish pink without buying it and unmortgaging those properties.

I will not trade with p1. They are the current board leader and I should not help them.

Vermont is useless to me because I already own the light blue set.

Indiana Avenue is unowned and costs $220. I can buy it with my $233 cash. If p4 buys it, they would hold two red properties and need Illinois from me to complete the set.

I will not trade Ventnor, Penn Ave, or Illinois. I will buy Indiana to block p4 from completing the red set. I am checking whether p3 would sell a property to raise cash.

I rejected offering cash for p3's dark blue properties. That would break their monopoly and leave me with a single weak dark blue, draining my survival cash.

I am now exploring a trade with p4. Their holdings include three railroads, Oriental, Connecticut, Electric, Kentucky, Atlantic, Marvin, Pacific, North Carolina, and Short Line. I could use Kentucky to complete the red set, but p4 would demand Illinois or something more valuable in return. Railroads would only provide income, not a monopoly.

I will end the turn without building, mortgaging, selling houses, or trading. The brown properties currently pay only $10 and $20 in rent, so the cash would be wasted.

Building three houses on each brown property would cost $200 and leave only $33 cash. The expected rent from p4 landing there is roughly $12.5, so the return is far worse than the cost. A roll of 10 lands on Mediterranean Avenue, and a roll of 12 lands on Baltic Avenue.

Selling houses would only raise cash to $283, but that would reduce future rent without immediate benefit. Mortgaging properties is unnecessary since I have no debt and no urgent need for cash.

Mortgaging would cost 10% interest to unmortgage and reduce the value of any future trade. The current rent from those properties is small but free cash, so they should stay unmortgaged.

p4 could build five houses on the yellow properties for $750, leaving only $4 cash. Their total mortgageable assets would reach roughly $1689.

A three-house yellow set would generate $800 to $850 in rent, instantly killing every opponent. A two-house green set would yield $600 to $750, which is equally lethal. Any trade that gives p4 a complete monopoly is fatal.

Trading Illinois would still leave p4 needing Indiana to complete the red set, so it is equally dangerous as giving up Ventnor. I am now looking for a trade that lets me complete a monopoly while blocking p4 from building.

I considered trading for both green properties. I would need to give up Ventnor or Illinois. That would let me build one house on each green property. The rent would be modest. p4 would still have enough cash to build a full yellow set.

I am weighing a trade that gives p4 Ventnor in exchange for both green properties. They would hold the yellow monopoly immediately, but building is restricted to each player's own turn. I am now considering whether this trade should happen now or wait until after my next turn.

The trade would let p4 build five houses on the yellow set before rolling. That would make the rent dangerous. p3 is already on Marvin Gardens and will not pay rent again until they leave.

p4 is already on Pacific (space 31), so they will not pay rent again this turn. p3 sits on space 29, and a roll of 2, 3, or 5 would land them on my green properties. If I hold a green monopoly with one house on one property, that single property could charge $130 to $150 in rent. p3 only has $76, so that would bankrupt them immediately.

A roll of 5 would land p3 on my green monopoly and charge $150 in rent. They could pay that by selling the house on Boardwalk for $100, so they would not go bankrupt. I would still collect the rent, but they would keep their assets.

A one-house green hit would leave p3 with enough cash to survive by selling their Boardwalk house. That would make my dark blue properties naked monopolies, but they would not bankrupt me.

The trade would leave me with only $33 and a weak green set while p4 holds five houses on yellow. I cannot afford to match that threat, since two-house greens cost $1200 and three-house greens cost $1800.

If p4 gave me all their cash plus both greens for Ventnor, I would have $987 and could build four houses. That would leave me with roughly $187 and a two-house, one-house, one-house green set. p4 would then hold the yellow monopoly with no cash and mortgage heavily to build three or four houses on yellows. Their two-house yellows would still yield about $450 each, which is comparable to my mixed green development.

p4 would never accept a trade giving them all their cash plus both greens for Ventnor. They have already offered $250, both greens, and Kentucky for Ventnor, but they want to keep cash to build yellows. That offer was rejected because it still lets them complete the yellow set.

I considered trading Penn Avenue and cash for both yellows. That would give me a yellow monopoly with one house, but p4 would immediately build three houses on their green set and kill me.

No trade with p4 is viable. They have five times my cash and can develop any monopoly they receive, while I cannot.

I will block all three of their monopolies and end the turn.

I am now checking whether p1 or p3 would sell a property cheaply. p1 is in jail with orange houses and no Get Out of Jail Free card. p3 has only $76 and one house on Boardwalk.

I considered offering all $233 cash for both dark blue properties. That would give me a monopoly with no cash to build on, and p4 would lose their only asset. They might accept if desperate, but they would still have no monopoly and I would be left with zero cash. A $200 offer for Park Place and Boardwalk is unlikely to succeed because the dark blue monopoly is their win condition.

A dark blue monopoly would leave me with only $33 and no cash to build. Rent from Boardwalk would be $200 and Park Place $70, which is too weak to threaten p4 or p1. p3 would also be left with no properties and almost no cash, so they would not help me. I cannot force p1 to mortgage or stop hoteling their winning orange set. I will end the turn.

I will keep my public message brief and avoid revealing too much strategy. I am considering encouraging p1 and p3 to view p4 as the main threat so they do not trade with him. p3 might be tempted by a monopoly offer from p4, but p1 has already refused similar deals.

p4 currently has no need for p3, though p3 might be useful to eliminate as a dark blue threat. A roll of 12 would land on St. James Avenue and charge $750, which is more than enough to bankrupt me even with full liquidation.

I considered buying Virginia for $160 to block p1 from completing a pink monopoly, but that would leave me with only one pink property while p1 still controls the other two mortgaged spaces. It would cost $87 in cash and provide no strategic benefit.

I am now considering buying Virginia to block p1 from completing a pink monopoly, though I would need to reserve $160 and might not cover other rent costs. Indiana is the more important unowned property at $220, but I am too far away to land there this turn.

I considered selling brown houses to raise cash for future purchases, but that would only yield $50 and leave liquidation unchanged. I can sell houses after the turn or when paying debt, yet buying property requires cash on hand at landing time.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $221 and am on ELECTRIC_COMPANY after paying $32 rent to p4. My holdings include one house each on MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE and BALTIC_AVENUE, plus three unmortgaged properties with zero houses. p1 has $314 and an orange monopoly with four houses each, plus mortgaged utilities.

p3 has a dark blue monopoly with one house on Boardwalk and zero on Park Place. p4 is in jail with a Get Out of Jail Free card, cash $966, and almost complete monopolies in yellow and green.

I will not trade Ventnor, Penn Avenue, or Illinois to p4. Indiana is still unowned and could complete my red monopoly. I can mortgage those three properties.

Building two houses on the browns would cost $100 and leave only $121, so that is poor ROI. Trading with p3 for dark blue properties seems unlikely to work because I have no non-blocking assets to offer.

Mortgaging all properties and selling houses would raise only $711. That is still short of the $750–$925 orange rent. I am effectively bankrupt if I land on any orange space.

I cannot buy unowned properties until I land on them. Selling houses would only make me weaker, and $221 is enough for small upcoming rents. Trading with p1 to weaken their orange monopoly is unlikely to work because I have no assets that complete their light blue set.

Blocking p3's dark blue would only reduce their threat marginally, since they are already cash-poor and their orange monopoly remains the real danger. Trading with p4 is unappealing because they hold $966 but would not pay much for my browns, and they still need Vermont to complete their light blue set.

p1 has $314 and can afford to hotel all three orange properties for $300. That would raise their rent to $950–$1200, which is catastrophic for me. I need to find a way to stop this.

I cannot stop p1 from building houses on their own turn. From ELECTRIC_COMPANY, the next roll will land on Virginia, States, St Charles, Illinois, B&O, Atlantic, Ventnor, or Water Works. None of these are orange spaces, so I am safe from immediate orange rent for now.

I can buy Virginia for $160 or B&O for $200 with my current cash, so I will not mortgage anything. I am now considering a trade with p3.

I am now considering buying Park Place from p3. They have only one house on Boardwalk, which may prevent trading that property. Park Place has no houses and could be tradeable. I would need to sell my own brown houses first.

I am reconsidering the trade with p3. If I buy Park Place, I would break their dark blue monopoly. But if p3 goes bankrupt, they could transfer those properties to p1 or p4 and give them both the dark blues and the orange monopoly. Keeping p3 alive might be better than acquiring one dark blue property.

I cannot afford to buy Park Place for $350. Trading Illinois to p1 or p3 would block p4 from completing the red monopoly, but it would also sever my own red path and leave me without a red blocker. I still cannot stop p1 from building houses on their own turn.

I cannot complete a red monopoly without trading p4 for Kentucky. My only viable win paths are to prevent others from completing monopolies, survive orange rent, or acquire a buildable monopoly. The brown set is already mine with one house each, but adding more houses would cost too much for the tiny rent increase.

Building three houses on the browns would leave only $21, which is too little to survive orange rent. Hotels are an even worse investment.

I am now considering a pink set instead. If I buy Virginia and can acquire p1's mortgaged St Charles and States for cash, I would have a complete pink monopoly.

A pink monopoly would be a real win path. I would need to unmortgage p1's St Charles and States, then buy Virginia for $160. p1 has no cash left to pay the mortgage interest, so they are unlikely to trade those properties.

I am now calculating a fair cash offer for p1's mortgaged St Charles and States. Unmortgage costs $77 each, so the total is roughly $154. I would need to offer around $100–$150, but p1 may reject this because they still want to complete their own pink monopoly if they land on Virginia.

p4 in jail can reach Virginia on roll 4 from space 10, and p1 has no other pink properties to complete their set. This makes p4 a more immediate threat than p1 for acquiring Virginia.

I am now calculating the exact cash offer to p1 for St Charles and States. I must keep $160 in reserve to buy Virginia on roll 2, which is only a 1/36 chance. B&O on roll 7 would not complete my set because I lack other railroads.

I will not trade cash to p1 because that would let them hotel their oranges and kill me faster. I have no non-essential properties to offer, and giving away my brown monopolies or blockers would be fatal. The timing is awkward: p4 could still steal Virginia before I can buy it.

Trading with p4 is also unwise. They have $966 and could build heavily on any set they complete. Giving them a property that completes their yellow or green monopoly would be fatal. They cannot finish red without Indiana, which is still unowned.

I will end my turn. I cannot afford to build, mortgage, or trade away my brown monopolies. Even liquidating all properties would only raise $711, which is still below the $750–$925 orange rent.

I will hit the orange spaces in about two turns, before I can pass GO. I need roughly $750 to survive that rent, but I only have $711. Passing GO is not an option because the oranges are ahead of it.

I need $39 more to survive St James, $164 to survive Tennessee, and $214 to survive New York. I cannot collect rent before my next turn because the other players move first. I have already spent money on the electric company rent.

I suspect the engine auto-resolves rent without allowing me to mortgage or sell properties mid-debt. Even full liquidation would leave me $39 short of the $750 minimum orange rent, so bankruptcy is unavoidable.

Building houses would destroy my liquidation value because each house sells for only half its cost. I am now calculating how much cash I can raise by selling my two brown houses, which would bring in roughly $50.

Selling Ventnor to p1 or p3 would block p4's yellow monopoly without completing it, and I would gain cash. Selling Penn Avenue to p1 or p3 would block their green set, but giving it to p4 would complete it and kill me. This is the play.

p4 has roughly $1,165 in total mortgageable assets plus $966 cash. That is enough to build houses on the red set over several turns if they ever land on Indiana.

I will offer player 4 Illinois for $350, one step below the previous $450 rejection. If they decline, I can lower the price to $275 or try player 1 next. The earlier rejection showed both price sensitivity and strategic doubt, so a smaller discount may not be enough.

Player 4 has a Get Out of Jail Free card and will be released next turn, so they may move soon. I am also considering offering to sell Illinois to Gemini as a backup denial if player 4 rejects the $350 offer.

I will propose the trade to player 4 now. The message will warn that if they decline, I will sell Illinois to Gemini as a pure block to kill their red set. Player 4 should pay to prevent that. I am ready to submit the trade proposal.

Player 1 has no properties I can offer them for a monopoly. They already own light blue and mortgaged pink, so I have nothing to trade. They might accept $220 for Illinois purely as insurance against player 4's red set, but they are winning with oranges and may not see the value.

Player 1 will not pay $220 to block their own orange hotels. They prefer to bankrupt opponents with higher rent. I have no properties they desperately want. Other spaces like Pennsylvania Railroad, Kentucky, and Virginia are harmless, but chance and community chest cards could bring bad luck. Landing on Park Place from Electric Company is impossible in one roll.

Dark blue properties are unreachable this turn. Orange rent is the only lethal threat. I am checking whether any chance cards could land me on Boardwalk or Illinois.

I had the board spaces wrong. I am now mapping the correct positions to check whether any chance cards could land me on Boardwalk or Illinois.

Selling Illinois for $350 would leave me with about $571, which still falls short of the $950 threshold. The hotel problem remains unresolved.

I am refining the cash estimate after selling Illinois. The notes assumed Ventnor Avenue was mortgaged for $100, but standard Monopoly rules set it at $130. Selling the brown monopoly would yield only $100–$150, which is too little to survive the Tennessee or New York hotels. Combining that sale with selling Illinois would require two trades and still leave a gap. I will focus on the single best trade now to maximize cash for Illinois.

I will offer player 4 Illinois for $350, a 22 percent discount from the rejected $450. I will pitch the Indiana angle and the threat to sell to player 1 as a block. Player 1 would be forced to keep their orange properties at four houses, so the rent stays at $750 for St. James Place and $875 for Tennessee Avenue. This means surviving the cheapest orange hotel becomes feasible without needing to drain player 1's cash.

I calculated the exact price needed to sell Illinois to player 1. A $215 sale would leave them with only $99, which is too little to build any orange hotel. That price covers the cheapest orange rent of $750, but it still falls short of the Tennessee rent of $875 under the notes rule. Under standard rules, the same sale would cover the Tennessee rent by about ten dollars.

Selling Illinois to player 1 for $310 would leave them with only $4 and no ability to build orange hotels. My liquid cash would reach about $931, which covers every four-house orange rent. This would guarantee survival this turn and permanently block player 4 from completing the red set. I am now weighing whether player 1 will accept paying roughly $300 for a property that does not complete any set.

Player 1 is the strongest player with four-house oranges. A $300 sale would leave them with only $14, which is too little to build hotels. I am checking what spaces they could land on from Tennessee next turn. They could reach my Illinois for $220 or Ventnor for $160, but rolling 16 to Pennsylvania is impossible. Landing on one of my properties would be dangerous for them.

Player 1 would be bankrupted by modest rents after a $300 sale. They cannot afford the $18 Kentucky rent or the $26 Atlantic rent with only $14 left. Player 1 will not accept that price.

Player 1 would likely reject any trade that leaves them unable to pay likely rents. The maximum they might offer is $100–$150, leaving them with roughly $164–$214. Even that small cash reserve would still allow them to build one orange hotel, since the cost of a single hotel is only $100.

Player 1 will not pay enough to stop any orange hotels. Player 4 is the only viable buyer, but that sale would not prevent player 1 from building hotels. I am now considering selling the brown monopoly to player 1 for roughly $215 or more, since it still generates rent.

- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.
